newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik gvt, opposition sign peace accord in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Tajik gvt, opposition sign peace accord in Moscow.

text.p: MOSCOW, June 27 (reuter) - Tajikistan's embattled President Imomali Rakhmonov and Islamic opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri signed an historic peace agreement on Friday, aimed at ending four years of civil war in which tens of thousands of people have been killed.

The Kremlin press service said the signing took place in the presence of Russian President Boris Yeltsin and other foreign officials. It was Yeltsin's first public appearance since attending the summit of the Group of Seven leading industrialised nations in Denver last weekend.

"This day should go down as a remarkable page in the history of Tajikistan. It brings to an end one of the longest and bitterest conflicts and peace is descending on the long-suffering land of Tajikistan," the Kremlin press service quoted Yeltsin as saying.
A seven-month-old ceasefire has largely held but the sweeping accord -- brokered by Iran, Russia and the United Nations -- has taken months of tough negotiations.

The deal was endangered by last-minute wrangling over a stalled prisoner exchange and political power sharing. But Tajik officials and diplomats say the accord is the first real chance of peace in the mountainous former Soviet republic bordering Afghanistan and China.
Under the deal, the sides have agreed to a power-sharing arrangement before elections next year. They must rebuild a shattered inflation-hit economy and clamp down on armed criminal bands.
